content.text: {"title":"The Class That Was Rewritten: One Run Through attrs","premise":"Writing a Python class with a handful of data fields means hand-writing nine or more dunder methods — `__init__`, `__repr__`, `__eq__`, `__ne__`, ordering, hashing, pickling — and keeping them in sync forever. *attrs* offers to write them for you. The price is that a decorator gets to inspect your class body at import time and, for slotted classes, hand you back a *different class object* than the one you wrote. This story follows one real run of the README example: a class body with two annotated fields walks into `@define`, comes out as a finished, slotted, unhashable, convert-on-setattr-free class; an instance of it is compared, serialized to a dict; and finally a second class is conjured at runtime from nothing but two strings. The reader is the person who has to sign off on all of that: what is guaranteed, what is silently decided, and where it can bite.","chapters":[{"n":1,"title":"The Door, and What It Decides Before You Knock","trace_lines":[2,5],"data_in":"`class SomeClass` with annotations `a_number: int = 42` and `list_of_numbers: list[int] = Factory(list)`, handed to `@define` as `maybe_cls`","data_out":"`define.<locals>.wrap` calls `do_it(cls, auto_attribs=True)` — frozen-ness checked against the bases, `on_setattr` already replaced by `_DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR` (`pipe(convert, validate)`)","code":["src/attr/_next_gen.py:23-47","src/attr/_next_gen.py:389-427","src/attr/_make.py:3105-3107"],"inputs":["SomeClass class object (pre-attrs)","Factory(list) as the default of list_of_numbers"],"characters":["define","define.<locals>.wrap","Factory","_DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR","setters.NO_OP"],"facts":["`Factory(list)` is evaluated at class-body time and merely stores the callable and `takes_self=False`; nothing is called yet (trace line 2-3).","`define` defaults differ from `attr.s`: `slots=True`, `auto_exc=True`, `auto_detect=True`, `order=False`, `force_kw_only=False` — visible in the trace's argument list on line 4.","`wrap` mutates the decorator's own `on_setattr`: when the class is not frozen and the caller passed nothing, it installs `pipe(convert, validate)`, so by default assignment after construction re-runs converters and validators.","`wrap` walks `cls.__bases__` and, if any base has `__setattr__ is _frozen_setattrs`, inherits frozen-ness and forces `on_setattr = NO_OP`; if the caller had explicitly asked for an on_setattr hook, this combination raises `ValueError` instead of silently ignoring it.","`auto_attribs` was left `None`, so attrs guesses: it calls `do_it(cls, True)` first and only falls back to `do_it(cls, False)` if `UnannotatedAttributeError` is raised."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q1.1","question":"A convert-and-validate hook is now wired into every future attribute assignment. Does every instance pay for it, even though this class has no converters and no validators?"},{"id":"q1.2","question":"The auto_attribs guess is a try/except around the entire class build. What exactly triggers the fallback, and can a half-built class leak out of the failed attempt?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":2,"title":"Flags Become Policy","trace_lines":[6,30],"data_in":"`attrs(maybe_cls=SomeClass, repr=None, hash=None, init=None, slots=True, frozen=False, eq=None, order=False, auto_detect=True, collect_by_mro=True, on_setattr=<wrapped_pipe>, ...)`","data_out":"`ClassProps(is_exception=False, is_slotted=True, has_weakref_slot=True, is_frozen=False, kw_only=NO, collected_fields_by_mro=True, added_init=True, added_repr=True, added_eq=True, added_ordering=False, hashability=UNHASHABLE, added_match_args=True, added_str=False, added_pickling=True, on_setattr_hook=<wrapped_pipe>, field_transformer=None)`","code":["src/attr/_make.py:1469-1476","src/attr/_make.py:1478-1566","src/attr/_make.py:1256-1281","src/attr/_make.py:1327-1350","src/attr/_make.py:2902-3061"],"inputs":["the class object","the resolved decorator flags from chapter 1"],"characters":["attrs","_determine_attrs_eq_order","_determine_whether_to_implement","_has_own_attribute","ClassProps","ClassProps.Hashability","ClassProps.KeywordOnly"],"facts":["`auto_detect=True` means every `None` flag is resolved by asking `_has_own_attribute(cls, dunder)` — a check of `cls.__dict__` only, so an inherited `__eq__`/`__init__` does *not* stop attrs from writing its own (trace lines 15-26 show `__eq__`, `__ne__`, `__init__` all absent).","Hashability is derived, not asked for: `hash is None` + `eq True` + `frozen False` ⇒ `UNHASHABLE`. The class will be deliberately made un-hashable, matching Python's rule that customizing equality invalidates identity hashing.","`added_pickling` defaults to the value of `slots`, so slotted classes get `__getstate__`/`__setstate__` written unless `auto_detect` finds the user's own.","`cache_hash=True` with a non-hashable outcome is rejected with `TypeError` before any class is built — a road not taken here because `cache_hash=False`.","The resolved `ClassProps` is not merely internal bookkeeping: `_ClassBuilder` stores it on the class as `__attrs_props__`, which is what `attrs.inspect()` later reads back.","`repr_ns` is deprecated and would emit a `DeprecationWarning`; it was `None` here."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q2.1","question":"`hashability=UNHASHABLE` is a decision made for the user. What is physically done to the class, and can a base class's `__hash__` survive it?"},{"id":"q2.2","question":"`added_pickling=True` was chosen because the class is slotted. What exactly gets written, and what does it do with state it doesn't recognize?"}],"answers":[]},{"n":3,"title":"Harvesting the Fields","trace_lines":[31,68],"data_in":"`_transform_attrs(cls, these=None, auto_attribs=True, kw_only=KeywordOnly.NO, collect_by_mro=True, field_transformer=None)` over a class whose `__dict__` holds `42`, a `Factory`, and a method","data_out":"`_Attributes(attrs=(Attribute(name='a_number', default=42, type=int, alias='a_number'), Attribute(name='list_of_numbers', default=Factory(list), type=list[int], alias='list_of_numbers')), base_attrs=[], base_attrs_map={})` wrapped in a generated `SomeClassAttributes` tuple subclass","code":["src/attr/_make.py:381-506","src/attr/_compat.py:17-34","src/attr/_make.py:295-310","src/attr/_make.py:104-214","src/attr/_make.py:2594-2626","src/attr/_make.py:320-350","src/attr/_make.py:266-284"],"inputs":["cls.__dict__ values (42, Factory(list), hard_math)","`_get_annotations(cls)` → {'a_number': int, 'list_of_numbers': list[int]}"],"characters":["_transform_attrs","_get_annotations","_is_class_var","attrib","_CountingAttr","Attribute.from_counting_attr","_collect_base_attrs","_default_init_alias_for","_make_attr_tuple_class"],"facts":["In `auto_attribs` mode the *annotations* drive the field list; a bare class attribute without an annotation is invisible, and plain values (`42`) are auto-wrapped by `attrib()` into a `_CountingAttr` (trace lines 37-50).","`_is_class_var` decides ClassVar-ness by **string matching** the annotation against `('typing.ClassVar', 't.ClassVar', 'ClassVar', 'typing_extensions.ClassVar')` — deliberately avoiding evaluation of string annotations, at the cost of being fooled by unusual aliasing.","The `UnannotatedAttributeError` that chapter 1's guess relies on is raised right here: any `attr.ib()`/`field()` in the class body without an annotation is collected into `unannotated` and rejected. The exception escapes before any class is created, so the retry in `wrap` starts from the untouched original class — nothing has been mutated yet.","Because `collect_by_mro=True` (set unconditionally by `define`), base-class fields are gathered by reversed MRO and deduplicated, keeping only the freshest definition. `define` users never get the legacy ordering bug of issue #428.","Any field without an explicit alias gets `alias = name.lstrip('_')` and `alias_is_default = True`, written in via `object.__setattr__` because `Attribute` is frozen. This happens *before* `field_transformer` runs so hooks see usable aliases.","After the (absent) `field_transformer`, attrs enforces that no mandatory non-kw-only field follows one with a default — a `ValueError` at import time, not a `TypeError` at call time."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q3.1","question":"Every field now carries an `alias` equal to its name minus leading underscores. Where does that string actually surface where a caller can see it?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.2","answer":"`UnannotatedAttributeError` is raised inside `_transform_attrs`, before the builder touches the class; the `define.wrap` retry therefore re-enters with `auto_attribs=False` against a pristine class."}]},{"n":4,"title":"The Hook That Quietly Removed Itself","trace_lines":[69,71],"data_in":"the `_Attributes` tuple plus `ClassProps`, inside `_ClassBuilder.__init__`","data_out":"a builder holding `_cls_dict = {'__attrs_attrs__': (...), '__attrs_props__': ClassProps(...), '__getstate__': slots_getstate, '__setstate__': slots_setstate}` and `self._on_setattr` reset to `None`","code":["src/attr/_make.py:676-778","src/attr/_make.py:1025-1064"],"inputs":["attrs tuple from chapter 3","props.on_setattr_hook = pipe(convert, validate)"],"characters":["_ClassBuilder","_DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR","slots_getstate","slots_setstate","_HASH_CACHE_FIELD"],"facts":["The builder scans every field for a validator or converter; because `SomeClass` has neither, the class-level `pipe(convert, validate)` hook is dropped (`self._on_setattr = None`). The optimization applies only to the three known hooks `_DEFAULT_ON_SETATTR`, `setters.validate`, `setters.convert` — a custom callable is always kept.","`__attrs_attrs__` and `__attrs_props__` are placed on the class, which is the entire public introspection surface other tools (and `fields()`, `has()`, `inspect()`) rely on.","`slots_setstate` accepts both the modern dict state and a legacy tuple (pre-22.2.0 pickles), and silently skips names missing from the state — a slotted instance unpickled from an older/partial payload can come back with unset slots rather than an error.","If hash caching were enabled, `slots_setstate` would reset `_attrs_cached_hash` to `None` so a restored object recomputes rather than trusting a serialized hash (GH #613).","For frozen classes the builder would instead install `_frozen_setattrs`/`_frozen_delattrs` here and mark `_wrote_own_setattr`; that branch was not taken."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q4.1","question":"Nothing executable has been produced yet — `__repr__`, `__eq__`, `__init__` don't exist. When and how do the strings become functions, and against which namespace?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q1.1","answer":"No. Because no field has a converter or a validator, `_ClassBuilder.__init__` sets `self._on_setattr = None`, so the convert+validate hook is discarded before any `__setattr__` is written."},{"id":"q2.2","answer":"`_make_getstate_setstate` returns `slots_getstate`/`slots_setstate` over the non-`__weakref__` field names; `slots_setstate` tolerates tuple state and missing keys."}]},{"n":5,"title":"Repr, Equality, and a Deliberate Absence","trace_lines":[72,85],"data_in":"the builder with two `Attribute`s","data_out":"two queued snippets — a `__repr__` script with globs `{_compat, AttributeError, NOTHING}` and an `__eq__` script — plus `cls_dict['__ne__'] = __ne__` and `cls_dict['__hash__'] = None`; `add_setattr` returned without writing anything","code":["src/attr/_make.py:1004-1012","src/attr/_make.py:1852-1906","src/attr/_make.py:1150-1162","src/attr/_make.py:1742-1776","src/attr/_make.py:1174-1224","src/attr/_make.py:1066-1068","src/attr/_make.py:1730-1739"],"inputs":["props.added_repr / added_eq / added_ordering","builder._on_setattr (now None)"],"characters":["_ClassBuilder.add_repr","_make_repr_script","_ClassBuilder.add_eq","_make_eq_script","__ne__","_ClassBuilder.add_setattr","_ClassBuilder.make_unhashable","_compat.repr_context"],"facts":["The generated `__repr__` guards against infinite recursion using a thread-local set of `id(self)` (`_compat.repr_context.already_repring`); a self-referential object renders as `...` rather than blowing the stack. The thread-local deliberately lives in `_compat` so generated functions don't hold a direct reference to it, which would break cloudpickle.","`__eq__` begins with `if other.__class__ is not self.__class__: return NotImplemented` — equality is type-exact, so a subclass instance never compares equal to its base, by design.","`__ne__` is a plain shared function that forwards `NotImplemented` from `__eq__` rather than inverting it.","`add_setattr` iterates the fields, finds no per-field `on_setattr` and a class hook of `None`, so `sa_attrs` is empty and it returns `self` immediately: **this class gets no custom `__setattr__` at all** — assignments are ordinary slot writes.","`make_unhashable` sets `cls_dict['__hash__'] = None`, which makes `hash(instance)` raise `TypeError`. attrs only *adds*; if a base class defined a real `__hash__`, this `None` shadows it for this class but attrs never reaches up the MRO to remove anything.","`add_str` would raise `ValueError` if a `__str__` were requested without a `__repr__`; `added_str` was False here."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q5.1","question":"`__eq__` short-circuits on exact class identity. What does that mean in practice for the comparisons the scenario actually performs?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q2.1","answer":"`make_unhashable` writes `__hash__ = None` into the class dict, so instances raise `TypeError` when hashed; it shadows rather than deletes any inherited `__hash__`."}]},{"n":6,"title":"Writing the Initializer, Line by Line","trace_lines":[86,96],"data_in":"`_make_init_script(cls, attrs, pre_init=False, post_init=False, frozen=False, slots=True, cache_hash=False, base_attr_map={}, is_exc=False, cls_on_setattr=None, attrs_init=False)`","data_out":"script `def __init__(self, a_number=attr_dict['a_number'].default, list_of_numbers=NOTHING): ... self.list_of_numbers = __attr_factory_list_of_numbers()`, globs containing `NOTHING`, `attr_dict`, `__attr_factory_list_of_numbers` **and the whole defining module's `__dict__`**, annotations `{'a_number': int, 'list_of_numbers': list[int], 'return': None}`","code":["src/attr/_make.py:2030-2096","src/attr/_make.py:2187-2448","src/attr/_make.py:2099-2184","src/attr/_make.py:1085-1108"],"inputs":["the two Attributes with their defaults and aliases","sys.modules[cls.__module__].__dict__"],"characters":["_make_init_script","_attrs_to_init_script","_determine_setters","_assign","Converter","NOTHING"],"facts":["The parameter names in the signature come from `a.alias`, not `a.name` — this is where chapter 3's underscore stripping becomes the public `__init__` contract.","A plain default is referenced indirectly as `attr_dict['a_number'].default`, so the `Attribute` object stays the single source of truth; a `Factory` default instead becomes `arg=NOTHING` plus an `if arg is not NOTHING: ... else: self.x = __attr_factory_x()`, which is why each instance gets a *fresh* list rather than a shared one.","Because the class is neither frozen nor hash-caching, `_determine_setters` returns the plain `_assign` strategy: the generated body is literally `self.a_number = a_number`. Frozen classes would instead go through a cached `object.__setattr__` or direct `__dict__` writes.","`_make_init_script` updates the generated function's globals with `sys.modules[cls.__module__].__dict__` so that `typing.get_type_hints(C.__init__)` can resolve string annotations. This means the generated `__init__` closes over a snapshot of the defining module's namespace — a deliberate trade of namespace purity for working type resolution.","Validators, when present, are emitted as a single `if _config._run_validators is True:` block after all assignments, so validators see a fully populated instance and can be globally disabled at runtime.","`init=False` on the decorator would route the identical script to `__attrs_init__` instead, leaving the user's own `__init__` in place."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q6.1","question":"The initializer's globals now include every name in the defining module. Is that live, and what is the blast radius if the module later rebinds a name?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q3.1","answer":"The alias is used verbatim as the `__init__` parameter name in `_attrs_to_init_script` (`arg_name = a.alias`), which is why `_x` becomes `x` in the public signature."}]},{"n":7,"title":"Two Protocols, Added Only If Vacant","trace_lines":[97,106],"data_in":"`_has_own_attribute(cls, '__replace__')` → False, `_has_own_attribute(cls, '__match_args__')` → False","data_out":"`cls_dict['__replace__'] = <function SomeClass.__replace__>` and `cls_dict['__match_args__'] = ('a_number', 'list_of_numbers')`","code":["src/attr/_make.py:1110-1123","src/attr/_make.py:1603-1607","src/attr/_make.py:589-644","src/attr/_make.py:1226-1253"],"inputs":["PY_3_13_PLUS","props.added_match_args"],"characters":["_ClassBuilder.add_replace","evolve","_ClassBuilder.add_match_args","_add_method_dunders_unsafe"],"facts":["`__replace__` (the `copy.replace` protocol, Python 3.13+) is a thin proxy to `attrs.evolve`, which rebuilds the instance **through `__init__`** using each field's alias — so `init=False` fields cannot be replaced and all validators/converters re-run on the copy.","Both additions are skipped when the class defines its own `__replace__`/`__match_args__` in its own `__dict__`; inherited versions do not count.","`__match_args__` only lists fields that are `init=True` and not `kw_only`, so positional pattern matching mirrors the positional part of `__init__`.","`_add_method_dunders_unsafe` rewrites `__module__`, `__qualname__` and `__doc__` on every attached method; the `_safe` variant (chosen at builder construction if the class lacks `__module__`/`__qualname__`) suppresses `AttributeError` instead."],"open_questions":[],"answers":[]},{"n":8,"title":"One compile(), One linecache Entry","trace_lines":[107,127],"data_in":"three queued snippets (repr, eq, init) with merged globs, filename `<attrs generated methods __main__.SomeClass>`","data_out":"`locs = {'__repr__': <function>, '__eq__': <function>, '__init__': <function>}`, each attached to `cls_dict` with attrs-branded `__qualname__`/`__doc__`, and `__init__.__annotations__` set","code":["src/attr/_make.py:782-798","src/attr/_make.py:231-263","src/attr/_make.py:217-228","src/attr/_make.py:1634-1641"],"inputs":["the snippet list accumulated in chapters 5-6"],"characters":["_ClassBuilder._eval_snippets","_linecache_and_compile","_compile_and_eval","_generate_unique_filename","linecache.cache"],"facts":["All snippets are concatenated and compiled **once** per class, and their globs dicts are merged into a single namespace — so a name used by one generated method is visible to all of them.","The source is registered in `linecache.cache` under a synthetic filename, which is what lets a debugger step through `__init__` and tracebacks show real source lines; collisions append a counter until a free filename is found.","`eval` is called on compiled bytecode built from strings attrs itself constructed from field *names*. Field names come from the class body or from `make_class` — attrs explicitly documents that validating identifiers is the caller's duty (see `make_class`'s warning), so a hostile or malformed name is an injection surface the library does not police.","The globs dict passed to `eval` becomes the function's `__globals__` — it is a live dict, but it was built by *copying* the module's `__dict__` at class-creation time, so later rebindings in the module are **not** seen by the generated code.","Attaching happens via per-snippet hooks (`_attach_repr`, `_attach_eq`, `_attach_init`) that pull the function out of the eval'd namespace and stamp it with the owning class's dunders."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q8.1","question":"These functions were compiled while the original class object still existed, and some of them (plus user methods) may hold it in a closure cell. The class is about to be replaced — what happens to those references?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q4.1","answer":"`_eval_snippets` joins all snippets, compiles them once under a unique synthetic filename registered with `linecache`, and `eval`s them into a merged globals dict; the resulting functions are then attached to `cls_dict`."},{"id":"q6.1","answer":"It is a copy taken at class-creation time, not a live view of the module: `globs.update(sys.modules[...].__dict__)` snapshots the namespace, so later rebindings in the module don't reach the generated `__init__`."}]},{"n":9,"title":"The Class You Get Back Is Not the Class You Wrote","trace_lines":[128,135],"data_in":"`cls_dict` (methods, `__attrs_attrs__`, `__attrs_props__`, getstate/setstate) plus the original `SomeClass` type object","data_out":"a brand-new `<class '__main__.SomeClass'>` with `__slots__ = ('a_number', 'list_of_numbers', '__weakref__')`, returned all the way up through `attrs` → `do_it` → `wrap` → `define`","code":["src/attr/_make.py:800-821","src/attr/_make.py:859-1002","src/attr/_make.py:509-558"],"inputs":["builder._cls_dict","builder._attr_names","props.has_weakref_slot"],"characters":["_ClassBuilder.build_class","_create_slots_class","weakref.ref","cached_property","_make_cached_property_getattr"],"facts":["Slotted classes cannot be retrofitted, so attrs builds a *new* type with the same name and bases and drops the field names from the class dict into `__slots__`. The original class survives only as `OriginalCls.__attrs_base_of_slotted__`, a weak reference to the replacement.","Because of the swap, methods that used bare `super()` or `__class__` carry a closure cell pointing at the *old* class; `_create_slots_class` walks `cls.__dict__.values()` (unwrapping class/staticmethods and properties) and rewrites any cell whose contents are the old class. This is the documented fix for issue #102 and the reason `functools.cached_property` and bare `super()` keep working.","Only non-inherited names are slotted, and slots already defined by a base are re-bound from `existing_slots` rather than redefined, so parent descriptors aren't shadowed incorrectly.","A `__weakref__` slot is added unless the class or an ancestor already has one — so by default slotted attrs instances stay weak-referenceable.","Consequences of the swap are real and documented: `object.__init_subclass__` fires for both the old and the new class, and the dead original lingers in `type.__subclasses__` until a GC pass (issue #407).","After construction, `build_class` calls `cls.__attrs_init_subclass__()` if one is *inherited* (not defined on this class) — attrs' replacement for the `__init_subclass__` hook it breaks.","The non-slotted path would instead call `_patch_original_class` and run `abc.update_abstractmethods` on the result."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q9.1","question":"Everything so far happened at import time. Once instances exist, is attrs still in the call path?"},{"id":"q9.2","question":"These instances have no `__dict__` at all. How does a helper like `asdict` find out what they contain?"}],"answers":[{"id":"q8.1","answer":"`_create_slots_class` iterates the new class's members plus the collected cached-property/`__getattr__` functions and rewrites every closure cell whose contents are the old class to point at the replacement."}]},{"n":10,"title":"An Instance, Briefly","trace_lines":[136,137],"data_in":"`sc = SomeClass(1, [1, 2, 3])`; `sc != SomeClass(2, [3, 2, 1])`","data_out":"`__ne__` → `True` (and, from the generated methods the trace doesn't re-enter, `repr(sc) == \"SomeClass(a_number=1, list_of_numbers=[1, 2, 3])\"`, `sc.hard_math(3) == 19`, `sc == SomeClass(1, [1, 2, 3])`)","code":["src/attr/_make.py:1730-1739","src/attr/_make.py:1742-1776","src/attr/_make.py:1852-1906"],"inputs":["two SomeClass instances"],"characters":["generated __init__","generated __eq__","generated __repr__","__ne__"],"facts":["The trace shows exactly one attrs-owned function in the whole instance lifetime of this comparison: `__ne__`. Construction, repr and `__eq__` are generated code living on the class, not library calls — the runtime overhead claim in the docs is visible here as an absence.","`__ne__` calls `self.__eq__(other)`, gets a real `False` (both operands are `SomeClass`), and returns `True`. Had the operands been of different classes, `__eq__` would return `NotImplemented` and `__ne__` would forward it, letting Python fall back to identity comparison.","`sc == SomeClass(1, [1, 2, 3])` holds because `__eq__` compares field values with `==`, field by field, in a single `and` chain — not by building tuples, which also means uncomparable values like `math.nan` behave as they would in hand-written code.","`hard_math` is untouched user code: attrs added methods around it and never wrapped it."],"open_questions":[{"id":"q10.1","question":"All of this machinery ran off a class body written by hand.
